notes.title: Dev Diary #3: Art Direction
notes.content:
[h1][b]Hi everyone, welcome to our new Dev Diary for Never's End![/b][/h1][p]I'm Ryan, the game director, and this time I'll be talking about the game's [b]art direction[/b] and the reasoning behind our design and artistic choices.[/p][p]When shaping the world of [i]Never’s End[/i], it has been important to find the right balance between [i][b]cute[/b][/i] and [b][i]dangerous[/i][/b]. It's a deep tactics game with several dark themes, and I wanted the aesthetic to have an element of maturity while also being more inviting than most tactics games of this complexity. We have placed a strong focus on creating a game with deep systems that's also accessible to a wider audience, and the visual design is an integral part of this goal. One of our earliest guiding references was imagining what “Chibi Bloodborne” might look like. This is most apparent in some of our earliest concepts for weapons and outfits.  [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45645341/db5b4261052cfe7dd7363596b804450e88bf71d8.png"][/img][/p][h1]Practical Armor[/h1][p]A core principle of our outfit design is [b]practicality[/b]. Armor and clothing should look functional and defensive rather than ornamental or revealing. We avoid designs that expose unnecessary skin or lean into a “sexy” fantasy style. Instead, every outfit should immediately communicate protection, weight, and material. This [b]visual clarity[/b] is especially important in combat. Attacks can strike either the head or the body, which are respectively protected by your clothing or hat, and damage is affected by the material of those items. A club is going to do more damage to metal armor than to cloth, and thus it needs to be obvious whether a piece of gear is made from linen, leather, or iron. For example, pairing a leather shirt with metal boots would create confusion about what the body is protected by because you equip your shirt, pants, and boots as one item. In contrast, metal armor with leather boots is more clearly a metal item because the largest visual element (the torso) is also the heavier weight material.[/p][h1][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45645341/3b63ef102de7652403770233fd0827dd8fb326d8.png"][/img][/h1][h1]A Blend of East and West[/h1][p]While [i]Never’s End[/i] is set in a medieval world, we’ve worked hard to avoid falling into a “generic fantasy” look. I wanted the designs to feel [b]familiar yet distinct[/b] to our world. We draw inspiration from a mix of [b]European[/b] and [b]East Asian[/b] influences, creating a world that naturally echoes the atmosphere of [b]classic JRPGs[/b], which take place in European-inspired settings while still retaining hints of cultural influence from where they were developed.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45645341/96899901f198168342d3886f3088a999447c0609.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45645341/15c86d0b6830a92b92680c22a796cc7f602393a3.png"][/img][/p][h1]Magic and Mystics[/h1][p]Magic in [i]Never’s End[/i] doesn’t take the form of flashy spellcasting. Instead, it reflects a [b]connection[/b] with the [b]laws of nature[/b]. A practitioner might manipulate heat or influence currents by modifying nature itself. Instead of casting fireball spells, you manifest the conditions for fire. To better communicate this distinction, I wanted to pull our magical outfit designs away from traditional high-fantasy robes. Instead, we focus on designs that feel more connected to [b]mysticism[/b] and [b]occult symbolism[/b]. They create a more grounded look to match our science-based supernatural powers. [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45645341/ba73a09e1090046faff6b5720cc5cab0791b7d69.png"][/img][/p][h1]Outfits of the Golden Age[/h1][p]Before humanity lost its war against the Never, the world wasn’t as bleak. In its golden age, society was more cultured, powerful, and filled with artisans. Players get to see some glimpses of the past world through flashbacks, and the outfits from this era reflect that past [b]sophistication[/b] in their style and patterns. [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45645341/c47c180dfd52b30157cb6d3841552a9a4ae5e592.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45645341/86a41e785854ddba4e27c1845a98a3d21e137db6.png"][/img]
[/p][h1]Designing for the Grid[/h1][p]Our [b]grid-based combat system[/b] requires [b]clarity[/b] in design. Creatures and enemies are stylized with chunkier proportions to ensure they read well from above and at small scales. This works well with our goal to [b]mix[/b] the [b]cute[/b] and [b]creepy[/b]. Designs often have unsettling details within cute proportions. You might want to hold them, but on closer inspection, there is [i]something[/i] a little off...[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45645341/70c757b5411faaa29180965f5ec25bffea8a43ae.gif"][/img]
[/p][h1]Temples[/h1][p]Temples are focal points in the game world. The game begins at the last surviving human town near the [b]Fire Temple[/b], and you will hunt down the other temples to acquire more magic and uncover what happened when the world lost its battle to the Never. The designs of each temple combine [b]details[/b] of [b]European churches[/b] with the [b]elemental symbolism[/b] of the [b]Godai[/b] from Japan. The Fire Temple, for instance, takes the form of a pyramid and features triangular design throughout the structure and as part of its followers’ outfits.  [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45645341/78d8b0d0f4835ba08a832e89943072cc52a2b8f9.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45645341/352ae8b349fa82c79d42d1c89417f99f376d323c.png"][/img][/p][h1]Form and Function[/h1][p]We aren’t just designing a world that looks cool. [b]We want a world that not only captures the eye but also serves our narrative and game design needs in a cohesive fashion[/b]. It needs to be visually clear what material every object is made from. If something looks like it can be picked up, we let players pick it up. If clothing provides protection, it needs to look protective. If an object blocks movement through the grid, it should appear large enough to do so. And the list goes on. Through this [b]balance[/b], we’re building a world that feels readable, unique, inviting, dangerous, and unsettling.[/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][p]And that wraps up our dive into the art direction of Never's End! We're very excited about how our world is coming together, and I hope this gave you all a better sense of what we're working on.
[/p][p]We still have plenty more to share, but in the meantime, we'd love to hear your thoughts. Which designs do you find the most appealing? How would you describe our art style? What would you like to see next?
[/p][p]Thank you so much for always following along. We're really grateful to share our journey with you all!
[/p][p]Be sure to hop onto our [url="https://discord.gg/hypersect"][b]Discord[/b][/url], subscribe to our [url="https://hypersect.us11.list-manage.com/subscribe?u=439d96db34a98bb5ec6a531cc&id=41a4d50bbf"][b]newsletter[/b][/url][b],[/b] drop a comment below, and follow us on our [b]socials[/b] for more updates and fun content![/p][p][/p][p]See you next time,[/p][p][i]- Ryan[/i][/p]

notes.title: Dev Diary #2 - Pushing
notes.content: [h2][b]Hello everyone and welcome (or welcome back) to our Dev Diary #2 for Never's End![/b][/h2][p]I'm Ryan, the game director, and one of my main goals with the design of [i]Never's End[/i] has been to [b]support player creativity and expressivity in combat[/b]. [/p][p]Wherever possible, we try to make all objects operate within a shared set of systemic rules, based on a common set of properties. This extends to our magic system, but it’s also important in more grounded interactions like [b]pushing[/b], which is what I want to talk about today.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]Positioning[/b][/h2][p]A lot of the game’s rules and calculations depend on how objects are positioned, and [b]pushing is your primary tool for rearranging the battlefield[/b]. If you are standing on higher ground than your enemy, you are more likely to land a headshot. If you are surrounded by multiple enemies, you are less likely to evade. If you are behind an obstacle, it might obstruct an incoming projectile and keep you safe. [/p][p]The list goes on, but one of the most important positional systems to be aware of is [b]engagement[/b]. Adjacent enemies become engaged and can't walk away from each other, but they can be pushed apart, which frees them up to move again![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45645341/540de36da13c17eb0705c66f845ae60bf003679f.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][h2][b]What Can Be Pushed?[/b][/h2][p]You can push items, crates, candelabras, chairs, tables, and just about [b]anything that isn’t rooted to the floor[/b], like a tree or building. You can push enemies, and you can also push your allies.[/p][p]All pushable objects have a [b]weight class[/b], which we use to balance the system. [b]Heavier objects cost more stamina to push[/b]. As a result, you can even push that giant boss you are fighting, but you might not be able to do much else afterwards.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]Systemic Interactions[/b][/h2][p]Pushing isn’t just about movement. It’s also about the interactions between what you push, and where you push it.[/p][h3][b]Impact Damage[/b][/h3][p]Push an object into a wall or another object of equal or greater weight, and it takes [b]guaranteed damage[/b] (there is no random roll to hit). And if you push it into an especially dangerous object such as a cactus or the spiked side of a barricade, you get additional [b]bonus damage[/b].[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45645341/6c83940bef71a5580c0acbdca573f9d3b4c1f9e7.gif"][/img][/p][h3][b]Chain Collisions[/b][/h3][p]If there are a series of objects lined up, [b]the collision will cascade down the line[/b]. Each one takes damage, but only the final object in the line is the one that actually moves, similar to a line of pool balls impacting.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45645341/2430e7cd63b7373f246e71dd3476ddb01de83f03.gif"][/img][/p][h3][b]Staggers[/b][/h3][p]If you push a character into a heavier object or just into a high terrain wall, they will be [b]staggered[/b]. Staggered characters are [b]unable to evade[/b] until the next turn, which makes it a great way to [b]increase your hit chance[/b] on a follow-up attack.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45645341/beba34cba5050a11646fbbfc6c0b0767df3cc6a4.png"][/img][/p][h3][b]Knockdowns[/b][/h3][p]When you push characters off of high ledges, they fall and become [b]knocked down[/b]. This takes them out of the fight for one turn![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45645341/5830594e2e8a9d3a88d804e29f8bd8210e652198.png"][/img][/p][h3][b]Bouncing[/b][/h3][p]When you try to push a character off a ledge, but there is another object in the spot where they would land, it causes a [b]bounce[/b]. The bounced-on character takes [b]damage[/b] according to the [b]weight[/b] of the pushed character that fell on them, and the pushed character will [b]bounce forward[/b] to the next location and possibly even bounce again. Bounces can create surprising strategies where you might want to push an ally off a ledge so that it damages enemies below while also safely reaching a new location.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45645341/77c4dbade17d2e1565459155ccd278935864aec6.gif"][/img][/p][h3][b]Status Transfer[/b][/h3][p]Things get more interesting when status effects are involved, because [b]anytime two characters collide[/b] from an impact or bounce, [b]certain status effects get transferred[/b] between them: [b]burning[/b], [b]oiled[/b], and [b]wet[/b]. Because these status effects then have their own sets of rules and interactions, this is a common place where high-skilled players can take advantage of very specific scenarios, but also where hilarious unintentional outcomes might appear.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45645341/5ec812dfceeee995be74c4239490c7c53e04a895.gif"][/img][/p][h3][b]Slipping[/b][/h3][p]The [b]terrain status[/b] you are pushing characters onto is also important to consider. [b]Ice[/b] and [b]oil[/b] are [b]slippery surfaces[/b] and let you push characters farther than usual.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45645341/aaffca78105e14606e61bafb3e77e0423f81039e.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][h2][b]Breaking Stances[/b][/h2][p][b]Pushing[/b] can also be used to knock characters out of different stances. If your foe has [b]raised their shield[/b], you can push them to lower it. The same goes for characters in a [b]resist stance,[/b] waiting for someone to approach, or characters in a [b]riposte stance,[/b] waiting to counterattack.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]Pushing, Pulling, Wind and Water[/b][/h2][p]So far, I’ve mostly been talking about [b]pushing characters away from you[/b]. That is how the standard push interaction works. But Never’s End provides [b]numerous ways to push[/b]. Some weapons allow you to [b]push from a distance[/b], such as the [b]pitchfork[/b] and [b]pike[/b]. Other weapons allow you to [b]pull characters towards you[/b], such as the [b]hoe[/b] and [b]halberd[/b]. Environmental forces like [b]wind[/b] and [b]water currents[/b] can be used to [b]push in any direction[/b]. While wind and water currents can be naturally occurring, they are most often due to magic, which can be very powerful when mastered. [b]Fire magic[/b] is your path to creating temperature changes that result in [b]wind[/b], which can be used to push characters left, right, forward or back, and it can do it at range! [/p][p][/p][h2][b]Player Freedom and Creativity[/b][/h2][p]Because Never’s End allows for so much [b]player freedom[/b], we are often discovering new [b]tricks and tactics[/b] in playtests that were not explicitly designed for. One of my favorite examples is [b]pushing to help your allies move into position[/b]. This can be a strong tactic in cases where movement is very costly, such as on [b]snow[/b] or [b]sand[/b]. You might have your archer on the back line push your warrior forward, getting them one step closer to the enemy before it’s their turn. This can result in landing additional attacks and give you an [b]early advantage[/b] in the fight.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]Continued Development[/b][/h2][p]The game isn’t finished yet, and we are always looking for [b]new ways to have our systems interact[/b], creating even more strategies and possibilities. One of our upcoming tasks is to experiment with characters standing on [b]webbed ground[/b] being [b]resistant to pushes from wind[/b] (some spiders create webbing as they move through the map). Time will tell how this feels and if it will be implemented permanently in the game, but I suspect it will be another interesting interaction that ties more systems together.[/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][p]That's it for this deep dive into pushing and how it fits into the various systems of [i]Never's End[/i]. Like many other mechanics in the game, it's easy to learn and use on its own, but it leaves a lot of room for experimentation once you start thinking more creatively.[/p][p]As development continues, we still have a lot of interactions and edge cases to explore, and I'm really excited to keep building upon systems that make combat feel dynamic and expressive.[/p][p]As always, [b]thank you so much[/b] for following along with the development and for all your support so far, it really means a lot to us.[/p][p]If you have thoughts, questions, or if you just want to speculate on possible strategies by using different mechanics, feel free to join our [url="https://discord.gg/hypersect"][b]Discord[/b][/url][url="https://discord.gg/hypersect"] [/url]or leave a comment below![/p][p]And if you want to see regular content about the game, such as videos showcasing mechanics, lore, design, and much more, be sure to subscribe to our [url="https://hypersect.us11.list-manage.com/subscribe?u=439d96db34a98bb5ec6a531cc&id=41a4d50bbf"][b]newsletter[/b][/url][url="https://hypersect.us11.list-manage.com/subscribe?u=439d96db34a98bb5ec6a531cc&id=41a4d50bbf"] [/url]and follow us on our [b]socials[/b]![/p][p][/p][p]Until next time,[/p][p][i]- Ryan[/i][/p]

notes.title: Dev Diary #1 - Origins and Inspirations
notes.content: [h1]Welcome to the first dev diary for Never’s End! [/h1][p]I'm Ryan, the game director, and in these dev diary posts, we'll be discussing everything from details about all aspects of the game - things like combat system design, our ever-growing soundtrack, behind-the-scenes technology, and our procedurally generated world. [b]Today, I'll be sharing some of the game's earliest inspirations dating way back to 2018 when development first started![/b][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45645341/d9f9d3a08689654b424fedfb04f5e1298edece07.jpg"][/img][/p][h1]Evolving World[/h1][p]I’ve wanted to make something with an evolving world for a while. Originally that was from a fascination with how things get repurposed by civilization over long time periods. I recall being in L.A. for E3 2014 where we were demoing Destiny multiplayer, and taking a day to visit the [url="https://www.getty.edu/visit/center/"]Getty Center[/url] (If you’re ever in L.A. you should visit. It’s free!) where they had an exhibit or [url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Ruscha"]Ed Rusha[/url] photographs. There was a series of photos showing the streets of L.A. changing over time, which reminded me of returning home to visit my family each year and seeing the details of my hometown grow and change, while the general shape remained the same. That [b]idea of the world moving on whether you're there or not[/b] felt like it would be interesting to explore in a game - the player might start doing something and then return later to see how someone else had finished or repurposed it.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45645341/0987fcc2b51e736acbb1d35e5f46cdec55407904.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][b]Originally, Never’s End would advance time by many many years with each death.[/b] NPCs would change and the shops inhabiting your towns would change. This was the origin of the rebirth mechanic that's still in the game today! However, we have since moved to a system where only a short time passes between deaths. We found that keeping familiar NPCs around better complimented some of the other game systems we had made, and it simplified some narrative problems to let us better focus our efforts. [/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45645341/0a5031e2e9f230af71999a414009c0dbc4ba5c44.jpg"][/img][/p][p]While your shops no longer swap out during the time you are away, we do still let the world grow and react to your progression. [b]Towns construct over time, terrain can erode, water can settle in new ravines, and the Never can spread.[/b][/p][p][/p][h1]Persistent Battlefields[/h1][p]If you’ve played our previous game, [url="https://www.inversusgame.com/"]INVERSUS[/url], you’ll know [b]I like the idea of player choices resulting in persistent effects on the landscape.[/b] INVERSUS doesn’t have randomized maps, but each shot fired changes the map so you get this butterfly effect where each game unfolds into a unique battlefield. [b]I wanted to bring some of those ideas into a tactics game.[/b] This extends back to playing [url="https://boardgamegeek.com/boardgame/105134/risk-legacy"]Risk Legacy[/url] (which was a large influence on INVERSUS) and my original idea here was that players would keep fighting on their same map again and again. The battles would adjust your map creating an ever-shifting playfield and overtime your board would look nothing like your friends', but it would be due to your player story and not due to random generation.[/p][p][/p][h3]Exploring the world 6 years ago: April 2019[/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45645341/2339901fe5e9668deb4ea57e68e8b1088dd0d77a.jpg"][/img][/p][h3]Exploring the world today: June 2025[/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45645341/07de452635a6a907d02ad40995ab3fe8259056b7.jpg"][/img][/p][p]As Never’s End grew to be a larger game, this shifted more towards you having a large number of interconnected battle grounds, each with their own history. As you learn each school of magic, you will gain abilities with more of these persistent side effects. The result is that [b]the world is rather stable in early parts of the game, but as you grow in power, you are more likely to have permanent effects. [/b][/p][p][/p][h1]Geomorphology Simulation[/h1][p][b]It was very important to me that we make a game you could replay and still face interesting decisions about what to do next.[/b] When making a game, you need to play it a lot - again and again - so I find this to be a feature that benefits both the player and the developer. This led me towards procedurally generated worlds. I also really liked that this made the game less solvable. [b]You can't just look up what to do next, but instead you need to engage with the systems and learn how the game works.[/b] Adding this to my prior goals of wanting the world to evolve and be modified by player actions, it meant everything needed be very dynamic and reactive.[/p][p][/p][h3]Debug view of procedural world generation and aging[/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45645341/e6e9de7d80b2565e27046386b532ff8e24971475.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][b]I needed to write systems for flowing water, eroding terrain, and dynamic weather with temperature, humidity and wind.[/b] This meant learning (or re-learning) all sorts of geology, geomorphology and meteorology. I found the interconnectivity of all these systems to be fascinating, and started reading books like [url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annals_of_the_Former_World"]Annals of the Former World[/url] and subscribing to every science podcast I could find because everything felt ripe for gameplay. I just needed to find the right simplified rule set which would later become the foundation of our magic system. [/p][p][/p][h3]Initial 2019 water simulation and current 2025 version[/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45645341/580a16f6d31090264703c461d79a45c7c6bdf122.gif"][/img]   [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45645341/06f69b8ed01b87bdef0d1d3c72a1a4b76a4958fb.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]I was also inspired by a talk that the developers of Legend of Zelda: Breath of Wild had given. They had similar goals of letting the player interact with simulations past standard physics gameplay and they referred to this as their Chemistry Engine. [/p][p][/p][h1]Hard Magic[/h1][p]Around the start of the project, I had been reading the [url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fifth_Season_(novel)"]Broken Earth[/url] series by [url="https://nkjemisin.com/"]N.K. Jemisin[/url] and the [url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mistborn"]Mistborn[/url] series by [url="https://www.brandonsanderson.com/"]Brandon Sanderson[/url]. Both of these had strong influences on the game, but I want to focus on Sanderson's concept of [url="https://www.brandonsanderson.com/blogs/blog/sandersons-first-law"]Hard Magic[/url]. [b]Hard magic refers to when a magic system has clear limitations understood by the reader.[/b] It becomes an interesting tool that characters can use to solve problems and is more grounded than Soft Magic which can basically do whatever the author needs. [/p][p][/p][p]Thinking along these lines is what made me want to try making [b]a magic system that was more foundational than I'd ever seen in a game.[/b] For example, our fire magic is very different from the series of arbitrary fire-themed spells seen in other RPGs. [b]In Never's End, you only learn one fire spell. It lets you move temperature from one location to another.[/b] It sounds simple, but because of the weather simulation, it explodes into a complex set of tactical options and you need to be smart about how you use it or you might just blow yourself off a cliff.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45645341/9072e6a154b9ca3f6a17e91de5b1fa6b7bf220e6.gif"][/img]          [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45645341/76979a9919e2b5b17d57fc160783d1024f9e57eb.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]That's all for today. Let us know what parts of the game you want to hear about next in the comments, and join [url="https://discord.gg/hypersect"]our Discord server[/url] if you want to discuss the above![/p][p][/p][p][i]- Ryan[/i][/p]

notes.title: ⚔️ Never’s End at BitSummit the 13th! ⚔️
notes.content:
[h2]We’re thrilled to share that [b]Never's End[/b] will be at [b]BitSummit the 13th[/b] in Kyoto next month! 🦇[/h2][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45645341/04c6b183cbab2ab986b93d8fd53d4c681a5fc919.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45645341/72eb8768dee0ef82ce02537c509c07e535815e1f.png"][/img][/p][h3]If you’re attending, come try our [b]very first playable demo[/b] at [b]Booth 3F-D57[/b] in [b]Miyako Messe[/b] (Kyoto International Exhibition Hall).[/h3][p][/p][p]What to expect:[/p][list][*][p]A short demo we prepared for you 🎮[/p][/*][*][p]A hands-on taste of the game’s combat and world 🌎[/p][/*][*][p]A chance to chat and share your feedback with us 💬[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p]📅 When: [b]July 18–20[/b][/p][p]📍 Where: [b]Miyako Messe[/b] (Kyoto International Exhibition Hall), [b]Booth 3F-D57[/b][/p][p][/p][p]More about BitSummit: [url="https://bitsummit.org/en/game/nevers-end-2/"]Official game page[/url] [/p][h3]

[hr][/hr]If you can’t make it to Kyoto, you can still follow our journey by [b]wishlisting Never's End[/b]:[/h3][p][dynamiclink href="http://store.steampowered.com/app/1999930"][/dynamiclink][/p][p]Don't forget to join our [url="https://discord.gg/Hypersect"]Discord server[/url] and our [url="https://hypersect.us11.list-manage.com/subscribe?u=439d96db34a98bb5ec6a531cc&id=41a4d50bbf"]Mailing list[/url] for more updates![/p][p][/p][p]Thanks for all the support, we can’t wait to see you there![/p][p][/p][p][i]- The Hypersect Team[/i][/p]

notes.title: Announcing our new game, Never's End!
notes.content:
[h2][b]Announcement Trailer[/b][/h2]

We're super excited to finally reveal [b]Never's End[/b], a turn-based tactical RPG set in a dark fantasy world that mixes Eastern and Western elements, with captivating, pixel-art like 3D graphics, a compelling story, and addictive gameplay. It will be available both on Steam and PS5!

[h2]Check out the announce trailer below:[/h2]

[previewyoutube=OkBd9ygZg8E;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3][b]Wishlist now[/b][/h3]

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1999930

[hr][/hr]
In [b]Never's End[/b] you return from death into the midst of a global cataclysm. In the ruins of a once-thriving civilization, a single village remains standing—an island of safety in a world devoured by the creeping darkness of the Never.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45645341/f911617b1486407491e96732020c4e010af6fe49.gif[/img]

You are humanity’s last hope: an undying warrior spirit, embodied in living silver, with the strength to face the Never’s endless hordes. Possess townsfolk to use them as living weapons, wield the forces of nature to reshape the battlefield, and lead mankind back from the brink of extinction.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45645341/f68aa286ffcf7f0503f1a551daa526d61650f342.gif[/img]

[h3][b]Key Features[/b][/h3]
[list]
[*][b]Control wind, weather, fire, water, and earth in a groundbreaking elemental magic system that obeys real physical principles[/b], granting unparalleled influence over a deeply simulated environment.

[*][b]Explore an open, fully traversable, and procedurally generated world.[/b] There are no instanced battles and no one path to victory. You decide your path and travel through the same world in and out of combat.

[*][b]Inhabit the bodies of townsfolk and use them as living weapons[/b], trading their lives for strength in a possession-based party system.

[*][b]The world is your weapon[/b]: every object, every piece of terrain, and every element of the weather system follows consistent physical and magical rules, creating new emergent tactics to discover at every turn.

[*][b]Over 150 explorable locations[/b] across [b]10 distinct biomes[/b], with 15 unique monsters and 8 powerful bosses.

[*][b]Over 35 armors[/b], [b]30 hats[/b], [b]40 weapons[/b], [b]5 shields[/b], and [b]60 secondary items[/b], to customize your possessed vessels with.

[*][b]Over 20 hairstyles[/b], [b]10 character backgrounds[/b], and [b]30 randomized character traits[/b] to ensure no two adventures are the same.
[/list]

[hr][/hr]
[h3][b]About us:[/b][/h3]
We are [b]Hypersect[/b], a small game studio with a never-ending love for making videogames. 
During the MIX Summer Game Showcase on June 3 we finally unveiled the announcement trailer for our upcoming title, [b]Never's End[/b]. We have been working on Never's End for 7 years now, and what started as a solo project turned into a dedicated team effort. 
We are currently still hard at work on the game, so we can't give you a release date yet, but we're excited to embark on this journey with you all!
